narrative.overview:
Trolley is a calm, capable desktop workbench for planning the same task from four useful perspectives. Its identity combines the supplied three-stroke mark, locally bundled Manrope Variable, warm chalk and ink neutrals, clear coral actions, and restrained sand-gold highlights. Brand expression is precise and quiet because this is an Operate-mode interface built for long working sessions.

The established architecture remains central: a dark project rail frames one flexible workspace, while Board, Timeline, Matrix, and List present a single canonical task model. Compact information, tonal layering, clear focus, and responsive reflow preserve scanability without turning the product into a field of generic floating cards.
keyCharacteristics: The supplied three-stroke Trolley mark and compact Manrope wordmark.
Warm chalk and near-black themes with exact, contrast-safe counterparts.
One task identity and metadata model repeated across four planning views.
Coral for actions, with sand-gold reserved for major highlights.
Functional status colors reinforced by labels, icons, shape, or position.
A desktop-first shell that remains reachable in narrow app windows.

rules.name: The Exact Rail Rule
rules.body: The rail is `light-rail` in light mode and `dark-ground` in dark mode. Do not tint it toward blue, green, or gray.

rules.name: The Gold Rarity Rule
rules.body: Use sand-gold only for major highlights and text selection. Its restraint is what makes it meaningful.

rules.name: The Redundant Signal Rule
rules.body: Status and data colors always accompany a word, number, icon, pattern, progress measure, or stable position; color never carries meaning alone.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every type role uses exactly `"Manrope Variable", "Segoe UI", sans-serif`; hierarchy comes from the variable family's settings.

rules.name: The Full-Contrast Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Input and textarea placeholders use the theme's secondary text token without an additional opacity reduction.

rules.name: The One Record Rule
rules.body: Preserve the same title, status, priority, labels, dates, progress, and assignee as a task moves across every view.

rules.name: The Search Stays Put Rule
rules.body: At narrow widths, search reflows inside the project header and never floats over project identity or header actions.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: Resting tasks, lanes, tables, and timeline bars use borders and tonal layering. Add a shadow only when state or stacking requires it.

rules.name: The Four Radius Rule
rules.body: Choose from `sm`, `control`, `md`, and `lg` unless a true pill, circle, notch, milestone, or native icon tile requires an exception.

rules.name: The Mark Integrity Rule
rules.body: Preserve the supplied three-stroke geometry. Use the full lockup where the product can be named, the symbol alone in compact or loading contexts, and the light symbol on the dark native icon tile.

rules.name: The Sub-task Ownership Rule
rules.body: Keep sub-task descriptions editable and their ordered rows movable. When any sub-task exists, its aggregate state owns the parent task's progress and workflow completion state.

rules.name: The Stable List Move Rule
rules.body: Preserve the source row as a placeholder, label the destination in the floating summary, mark insertion without changing table geometry, and leave the completed move visible in manual order.

dos: Do preserve one task identity and metadata order across all four views.
Do use the supplied logo lockups according to surface and available space.
Do keep primary actions and gold selections legible with dark ink.
Do retain explicit placeholder, column-control, and scrollbar contrast.
Do keep project search in flow and all header actions reachable at narrow widths, including the shipped `800 x 650` window.
Do support pointer and keyboard task opening, keyboard drag alternatives, visible Matrix drag feedback, named collapsed controls, and reduced motion.
Do keep List row moves stable with a source placeholder, floating summary, named destination, insertion line, and `0.7rem` status counts.
Do keep sub-task descriptions editable, their order movable, and parent progress and workflow completion synchronized with checked items.
donts: Don't replace the shell with a generic floating-card dashboard or a field of unrelated rounded panels.
Don't use color alone to communicate priority, state, completion, danger, progress, or drag destination.
Don't use sand-gold as a routine accent or replace coral as the action color.
Don't introduce another type family or simulate a condensed display face.
Don't tint the rail away from its exact light and dark anchor values.
Don't weaken secondary text, placeholders, selection text, column controls, or scrollbars with additional opacity.
Don't collapse, transform, or remove the source List row while it is being moved; the table geometry must remain stable.
